questions.q: Which of the following best describes the meaning of political parties in a modern democratic state? 1️⃣ They are voluntary associations or organised groups of individuals. 2️⃣ Members must share the same political views. 3️⃣ They must aim to gain political power only through constitutional means. 4️⃣ Their primary desire is to work for promoting the national interest.
questions.e: According to the text, political parties are defined as voluntary associations or organised groups of individuals who share the same political views, try to gain power through constitutional means, and desire to work for promoting national interest.

questions.q: Consider the following types of political parties and their descriptions: 1️⃣ Reactionary parties — Cling to old socio-economic and political institutions. 2️⃣ Conservative parties — Aim at reforming existing institutions. 3️⃣ Liberal parties — Believe in the status-quo. 4️⃣ Radical parties — Aim at establishing a new order by overthrowing existing institutions. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Reactionary and Radical descriptions are correct. However, Conservative parties believe in the status-quo, while Liberal parties aim at reforming existing institutions.

questions.q: In the ideological classification of political parties, where do political scientists place "Liberal" parties?
questions.e: Political scientists place radical parties on the left, liberal parties in the centre, and reactionary/conservative parties on the right.

questions.q: With reference to the party system in India, which of the following political parties is categorized as a "Centrist" party?
questions.e: In the Indian context, the CPI and CPM are examples of leftist parties, the Congress is a centrist party, and the BJP is an example of a rightist party.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of countries and their respective party systems: 1️⃣ USA — Two-party system. 2️⃣ France — Multi-party system. 3️⃣ USSR (former) — One-party system. 4️⃣ Britain — Multi-party system. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: USA and Britain both have two-party systems. France, Switzerland, and Italy have multi-party systems. The former USSR had a one-party system.

questions.q: Which of the following factors contributed to the rise of a multi-party system in India? 1️⃣ Continental size of the country. 2️⃣ Diversified character of Indian society. 3️⃣ Adoption of universal adult franchise. 4️⃣ Peculiar type of political process.
questions.e: The text explicitly lists the continental size, social diversity, universal adult franchise, and the peculiar political process as factors giving rise to a large number of parties in India.

questions.q: Who described the Indian party system as the 'one party dominance system' or the 'Congress system'?
questions.e: Eminent political analyst Rajni Kothari preferred to call the Indian party system the 'one party dominance system' or the 'Congress system' due to long-term Congress dominance.

questions.q: According to the text, which of the following parties in India are noted for having a clear-cut ideology? 1️⃣ BJP 2️⃣ CPI 3️⃣ CPM 4️⃣ Indian National Congress
questions.e: The text states that except for the BJP and the two communist parties (CPI and CPM), all other parties do not have a clear-cut ideology and are ideologically closer to each other.

questions.q: Which characteristic of the Indian party system is reflected in the statement "there are political personalities rather than political parties in India"?
questions.e: This refers to the Personality Cult, where parties are organised around an eminent leader who becomes more important than the party and its ideology.

questions.q: In western countries, political parties are typically formed on the basis of socio-economic programmes. In India, many parties are formed based on which of the following "traditional factors"? 1️⃣ Religion 2️⃣ Caste 3️⃣ Language 4️⃣ Race
questions.e: Unlike western parties, a large number of Indian parties are formed on the basis of religion, caste, language, culture, race, etc..

questions.q: With reference to regional parties in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They were always confined to regional politics and never played a role at the national level. 2️⃣ Their significance in national politics increased due to the era of coalition governments at the Centre.
questions.e: While initially confined to regional politics, regional parties have come to play a significant role in national politics due to coalition governments.

questions.q: When did the practice of "defections" gain greater currency in Indian politics, leading to political instability?
questions.e: The practice of defections gained greater currency after the fourth general elections in 1967, causing instability at both the Centre and in states.

questions.q: Which of the following is a consequence of the lack of an effective Opposition in India's parliamentary democracy? 1️⃣ Check on autocratic tendencies of the ruling party. 2️⃣ Failure to provide a viable alternative government. 3️⃣ Inability to play a constructive role in nation building.
questions.e: An effective opposition is meant to check autocratic tendencies, but in India, the lack of a strong opposition has resulted in a failure to provide alternative governments and constructive nation-building roles.

questions.q: Who is responsible for registering political parties and granting them recognition as "National" or "State" parties in India?
questions.e: The Election Commission registers political parties for election purposes and grants recognition as national or state parties based on poll performance.

questions.q: What is a primary privilege granted to a "Recognised" political party that is not available to an "Unrecognised" party?
o: The right to form a coalition
questions.e: Recognition grants privileges like the allocation of reserved party symbols, provision of time on state-owned TV/Radio, and access to electoral rolls.

questions.q: For a political party to be recognized as a "National Party," it must fulfill certain conditions. Which of the following is one such condition?
o: It is recognised as a state party in at least four states.
It wins 5% of seats in the Lok Sabha from any one state.
It wins at least 10 seats in the Rajya Sabha.
It secures 10% of valid votes in two states in a general election.
questions.e: One of the conditions for national recognition is being recognised as a state party in four states.

questions.q: A political party can be recognized as a "National Party" if it secures 6% of valid votes in four or more states at a general election to the Lok Sabha or Assembly, and in addition, it wins how many seats in the Lok Sabha?
questions.e: To be a national party under the 6% vote rule, the party must also win four seats in the Lok Sabha from any state or states.

questions.q: To be recognized as a "State Party," what percentage of the total valid votes must a party secure in a General Election to the Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly of that state, according to the latest 8% rule?
questions.e: A party is recognised as a state party if it secures 8% of the total valid votes polled in the state at a General Election to the Lok Sabha or the legislative assembly.

questions.q: Consider the following conditions for recognition as a "State Party": 1️⃣ It wins 3% of seats in the legislative assembly or 3 seats, whichever is more. 2️⃣ It wins 1 seat in the Lok Sabha for every 25 seats allotted to the state.
questions.e: Both are valid conditions for state party recognition.

questions.q: How many national parties were there in India on the eve of the Seventeenth Lok Sabha general elections (2019)?
questions.e: On the eve of the 2019 elections, there were 7 national parties and 52 state parties.

questions.q: Match the following Political Parties with their Founders: 1️⃣ Indian National Congress — A.O. Hume 2️⃣ Communist Party of India — M.N. Roy 3️⃣ Bahujan Samaj Party — Kanshi Ram 4️⃣ Telugu Desam Party — N.T. Rama Rao. How many pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four matches are correct as per Table 79.1.

questions.q: In what year was the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) formed?
questions.e: The BJP was formed in 1980 by A.B. Vajpayee and L.K. Advani.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a regional party?
o: It aims to capture political power at the national level as its primary goal.
It generally operates within a particular state.
It desires greater regional autonomy for states.
It articulates regional interests and identities.
questions.e: Regional parties focus on local/regional issues and aim to capture power at the state level, though they may play a role at the national level via coalitions.

questions.q: The Samajwadi Party (SP) and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) are classified as which type of regional parties?
o: Parties with an all-India outlook but lacking a national electoral base.
Parties formed by a split in national parties.
questions.e: SP and NCP are examples of regional parties that have an all-India outlook but lack a national electoral base.

questions.q: Which of the following regional parties were formed due to a split in national parties? 1️⃣ Biju Janata Dal 2️⃣ Rashtriya Janata Dal 3️⃣ Trinamool Congress 4️⃣ YSR Congress
questions.e: All the listed parties (BJD, RJD, TMC, YSRCP) were formed by splits in national parties.

questions.q: Which of the following is a reason for the rise of regional parties in India? 1️⃣ Cultural and ethnic pluralism. 2️⃣ Economic disparities and regional imbalances. 3️⃣ Failure of national parties to meet regional aspirations. 4️⃣ Reorganisation of states on the basis of language.
questions.e: The text lists all these as reasons for the emergence of regional parties.

questions.q: How have regional parties impacted Centre-State relations in India?
o: They have demanded greater autonomy, making the Centre more responsive to regional needs.
They have abolished the role of Governors.
They have made the Central leadership less responsive to states.
They have led to the centralization of all powers.
questions.e: Regional parties have made a strong impact by demanding greater autonomy, making the central leadership more responsive to regional needs.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a "dysfunction" or negative role of regional parties? 1️⃣ Encouraging regionalism and communalism. 2️⃣ Resolving inter-state water disputes. 3️⃣ Focusing on populist schemes that affect the state economy. 4️⃣ Promoting national interest over regional interest.
questions.e: Negative roles include encouraging regionalism/communalism and focusing on populist schemes that hurt the economy. They are often blamed for the non-resolution of inter-state disputes.

questions.q: Under which Part of the Indian Constitution are the provisions regarding the electoral system located?
questions.e: Articles 324 to 329 in Part XV of the Constitution deal with the electoral system.

questions.q: Article 324 of the Constitution vests the power of superintendence, direction, and conduct of which elections in the Election Commission? 1️⃣ Parliament 2️⃣ State Legislatures 3️⃣ Office of President 4️⃣ Office of Vice-President 5️⃣ Panchayats and Municipalities
questions.e: The ECI conducts elections for Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. A separate state election commission deals with panchayats and municipalities.

questions.q: On what grounds can a person be declared ineligible for inclusion in the electoral roll according to Article 325?
questions.e: Article 325 states that no person is to be ineligible for inclusion in the electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or any of them.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.e: The 61st Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years, effective March 28, 1989.

questions.q: With reference to the power of making laws regarding elections, which of the following is correct?
o: State Legislatures can only supplement Parliamentary laws on state election matters not covered by Parliament.
Only Parliament can make laws for both Parliament and State Legislatures.
The Election Commission alone makes all election laws.
State Legislatures can make laws for state elections that override Parliamentary laws.
questions.e: State legislatures can make provisions for state elections only on matters not covered by Parliament; they supplement and cannot override Parliamentary law.

questions.q: Can the validity of a law relating to the delimitation of constituencies be challenged in a court of law?
o: No, the Constitution bars interference by courts in such matters.
Only if the Election Commission permits.
questions.e: The Constitution (Article 329) declares that the validity of laws relating to delimitation or allotment of seats cannot be questioned in any court.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court declare the provision for establishing an election tribunal (Article 323B) excluding court jurisdiction as unconstitutional?
questions.e: In the Chandra Kumar case (1997), the Supreme Court declared the provision excluding court jurisdiction in election disputes (under Article 323B) as unconstitutional.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls for a Parliamentary or assembly constituency?
questions.e: The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) is responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls for a constituency.

questions.q: Which officer is responsible for the actual conduct of elections in a specific Parliamentary or assembly constituency?
questions.e: The Returning Officer (RO) is responsible for the conduct of elections in the concerned Parliamentary or assembly constituency.

questions.q: Consider the following types of Observers deployed by the Election Commission: 1️⃣ General Observers — Ensure smooth conduct and free/fair elections. 2️⃣ Expenditure Observers — Monitor election spending of candidates. 3️⃣ Police Observers — Monitor force deployment and law and order. 4️⃣ Micro Observers — Observe proceedings at critical/vulnerable polling stations. How many of the above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four descriptions correctly identify the roles of the various observers nominated by the ECI.

questions.q: What is the maximum time gap allowed by the Constitution between the last session of a dissolved Lok Sabha and the recalling of the new House?
questions.e: The Constitution states there can be no longer than six months between the last session of the dissolved Lok Sabha and the recalling of the new House.

questions.q: When does the "Model Code of Conduct" for guidance of candidates and parties come into effect?
o: Only on the days of polling.
Immediately after the Election Commission announces the schedule of elections.
Immediately after the election results are declared.
questions.e: The Model Code of Conduct comes into effect immediately after the Election Commission announces the schedule of elections.

questions.q: How much time are candidates typically given to file their nominations after the election notification is issued?
questions.e: As per the formal process, candidates are given a week to put forward their nominations.

questions.q: What is the time limit for a validly nominated candidate to withdraw their nomination after scrutiny?
questions.e: Validly nominated candidates can withdraw their nominations within two days after they have been scrutinised.

questions.q: When must a candidate take an oath or affirmation before the authorized officer?
o: Immediately after presenting nomination papers and not later than the day before scrutiny.
At the time of counting votes.
questions.e: The candidate is required to make the oath/affirmation immediately after presenting nominations and not later than the day previous to the date of scrutiny.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the official election campaign period?
o: It ends 48 hours before polling closes.
It lasts for exactly one month.
It ends 24 hours before polling closes.
It begins only on the day of nomination.
questions.e: The official campaign ends 48 hours before polling closes.

questions.q: In which year did the Election Commission take the historic decision to use only Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for the Lok Sabha elections?
questions.e: After using them experimentally, the ECI decided to use only EVMs for the 2004 Lok Sabha elections.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of EVMs mentioned in the text?
o: Reduces the quantity of paper used.
questions.e: Advantages include eliminating invalid votes, faster counting, and being eco-friendly by saving paper. Ensuring 100% turnout is not an inherent function of the machine itself.

questions.q: To ensure accessibility, the Election Commission tries to ensure that a polling station is within what distance of every voter?
questions.e: Officials try to ensure there is a polling station within two kilometres of every voter.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of voters a single polling station is usually expected to deal with?
questions.e: The ECI tries to ensure that no polling station has to deal with more than 1200 voters.

questions.q: With reference to media coverage of elections, consider the following: 1️⃣ Opinion polls cannot be published starting two days before polling until the close of poll. 2️⃣ Exit poll results can only be published after half an hour of the end of polling on the last day.
questions.e: Both statements accurately reflect the ECI's stipulations regarding the publication of opinion and exit polls.

questions.q: What electoral system is used for elections to the Lok Sabha in India?
questions.e: Elections to the Lok Sabha are carried out using a first-past-the-post electoral system.

questions.q: Who has the jurisdiction to try election petitions since 1966?
questions.e: Since 1966, election petitions are triable by High Courts alone, with appellate jurisdiction lying with the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Which party won the most seats in the first Lok Sabha elections (1952)?
questions.e: In 1952, the Congress won 364 seats out of 489.

questions.q: Match the following Articles with their subject matter: 1️⃣ Article 324 — Election Commission 2️⃣ Article 326 — Adult Suffrage 3️⃣ Article 327 — Power of Parliament to make laws 4️⃣ Article 329 — Bar to interference by courts. How many are correctly matched?
questions.e: Table 81.2 confirms these article assignments.

questions.q: What was the primary purpose of the Representation of the People Act, 1950? 1️⃣ Allocation of seats in Parliament and State Legislatures. 2️⃣ Delimitation of constituencies. 3️⃣ Registration of electors and qualifications for registration. 4️⃣ Conduct of elections and election disputes.
questions.e: The 1950 Act deals with seat allocation, delimitation, and voter registration. The actual conduct of elections and disputes are covered by the 1951 Act.

questions.q: Which Act contains provisions relating to the registration of political parties and the conduct of elections?
questions.e: The 1951 Act contains provisions for the registration of political parties and the actual conduct of elections.

questions.q: The Delimitation Act of 2002 was enacted to set up a commission based on which census?
questions.e: The Delimitation Act, 2002 was enacted to effect delimitation on the basis of the 2001 census.

questions.q: Which Act regulates matters relating to elections to the offices of the President and Vice-President of India?
questions.e: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 regulates these specific elections.

questions.q: Which order provides for the specification, reservation, and choice of symbols at elections?
questions.e: The Election Symbols Order, 1968 provides for the allocation and recognition of symbols.

questions.q: Which committee was appointed in 1974 by Jaya Prakash Narayan to examine electoral reforms?
questions.e: The Tarkunde Committee was appointed in 1974 by JP during his "Total Revolution" movement.

questions.q: Which committee specifically examined the "Nexus between Crime and Politics" in 1993?
questions.e: The Vohra Committee (1993) examined the nexus between crime and politics.

questions.q: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) was primarily related to which of the following?
questions.e: The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with the state funding of elections.

questions.q: Who headed the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC) from 2000-2002?
questions.e: The NCRWC was headed by M.N. Venkatachaliah.

questions.q: Which reform was introduced before 1996 to prevent "non-serious candidates" from contesting elections to the Rajya Sabha?
o: Introducing the Elector's Photo Identity Card
Increasing the number of proposers to 10% of electors or ten, whichever is less
questions.e: In 1989, the number of proposers for Rajya Sabha nominations was increased to prevent non-serious candidates.

questions.q: In which year did the Election Commission decide to issue photo identity cards (EPIC) to electors throughout the country?
questions.e: The decision to issue EPICs was taken by the Election Commission in 1993.

questions.q: Under the electoral reforms of 1996, how are candidates classified for the listing of names on ballot papers? 1️⃣ Candidates of recognised political parties. 2️⃣ Candidates of registered-unrecognised political parties. 3️⃣ Independent candidates.
questions.e: Candidates are classified into these three categories, and their names appear in this specific order.

questions.q: A person convicted under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act of 1971 is disqualified from contesting elections for how many years?
questions.e: Conviction for insulting the national flag, constitution, or anthem leads to disqualification for 6 years.

questions.q: What is the prohibition regarding the sale of liquor in a polling area?
o: Liquor is only banned at public shops.
No sale on the day of result.
No sale for 24 hours before polling.
No sale for 48 hours ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of poll.
questions.e: Liquor sale/distribution is prohibited within a polling area for 48 hours ending with the conclusion of poll.

questions.q: After the 1996 reforms, what happens if a contesting candidate (not belonging to a recognised party) dies before polling?
o: The party can propose a new candidate within 7 days.
The election process starts all over.
questions.e: Now, the election is not countermanded on the death of a candidate. If the candidate was from a recognised party, the party gets 7 days to propose another.

questions.q: What is the time limit for holding a by-election after a vacancy occurs in a House?
questions.e: By-elections are to be held within six months of the vacancy.

questions.q: According to the 1996 reforms, a candidate is restricted to contesting from a maximum of how many constituencies at a general election?
questions.e: A candidate can contest from no more than two constituencies.

questions.q: What reform was introduced in 1997 to discourage frivolous candidates for the office of the President? 1️⃣ Proposers and seconders increased to 50 each. 2️⃣ Security deposit increased to ₹15,000.
questions.e: In 1997, proposers/seconders were increased to 50 for President (20 for VP) and the deposit was raised to ₹15,000 for both.

questions.q: Which class of voters was provided the facility to vote through proxy in 2003?
o: Service voters of the Armed Forces
questions.e: In 2003, proxy voting was provided to service voters belonging to the Armed Forces.

questions.q: Since 2003, candidates are required to declare which of the following in their nomination papers? 1️⃣ Criminal antecedents (convictions or pending cases). 2️⃣ Assets and liabilities of self, spouse, and dependents. 3️⃣ Educational qualifications.
questions.e: Candidates must furnish information on criminal cases, assets/liabilities, and education.

questions.q: Which of the following changes was introduced in Rajya Sabha elections in 2003? 1️⃣ Removal of domicile requirement for candidates. 2️⃣ Introduction of an open ballot system instead of secret ballot.
questions.e: In 2003, the domicile requirement was removed and an open ballot system was introduced to curb cross-voting.

questions.q: Under the 2003 reforms, what is the reporting threshold for political parties receiving contributions?
questions.e: Parties must report contributions in excess of ₹20,000 to the Election Commission to claim tax relief.

questions.q: Why were Braille signage features introduced in EVMs starting from the 2004 bye-elections?
o: To facilitate visually impaired voters to cast votes without an attendant.
To make the machines look more modern.
questions.e: Braille signage allows visually impaired voters to cast their votes independently.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the security deposit for candidates contesting Lok Sabha elections after 2009?
questions.e: In 2009, the deposit was increased to ₹25,000 for general candidates and ₹12,500 for SC/ST candidates for Lok Sabha.

questions.q: According to the 2010 amendment, which citizens living abroad are entitled to have their names registered in the electoral roll?
o: Only those living abroad for education.
Those who have acquired foreign citizenship.
Those who have not acquired the citizenship of any other country.
Only those who have a business in India.
questions.e: Citizens living abroad who have not acquired foreign citizenship are entitled to register in their resident constituency in India.

questions.q: What is the "None of the Above" (NOTA) option?
o: A way to cancel the entire election.
An option only available for NRI voters.
An option to reject all candidates in the fray while maintaining secrecy.
A vote that is given to the runner-up.
questions.e: NOTA allows voters to exercise their right not to vote for any candidate while maintaining ballot secrecy.

questions.q: What is the Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT)?
o: A machine used to print electoral rolls.
A tool for counting postal ballots.
An independent system attached to EVMs allowing voters to verify their cast vote.
questions.e: VVPAT prints a slip for 7 seconds showing the candidate's name and symbol to verify the vote was cast as intended.

questions.q: According to the Supreme Court ruling in Lily Thomas vs. Union of India (2013), what happens to MPs and MLAs on conviction for offences?
o: They are only disqualified if they are in jail.
They are given 3 months to appeal.
They can continue until the end of their term.
They are immediately disqualified from holding membership.
questions.e: The SC held that convicted lawmakers are immediately disqualified without being given a three-month appeal period.

questions.q: Why did the Election Commission decide to carry photos of candidates on EVMs and ballot papers after May 2015?
o: To avoid confusion among electorates where namesakes are contesting.
questions.e: Photos help voters distinguish between candidates with same or similar names.

questions.q: In the 2017 budget, the limit for anonymous cash donations to a political party was lowered from ₹20,000 to what amount?
questions.e: The limit for anonymous cash donations was lowered to ₹2,000 in 2017.

questions.q: With reference to Electoral Bonds introduced in 2018, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are bearer banking instruments without the buyer's name. 2️⃣ Only parties that secured at least 1% of votes in the last election are eligible. 3️⃣ They can be purchased by any foreign entity.
questions.e: Electoral bonds are bearer instruments for eligible parties (1% vote threshold). They can be purchased by Indian citizens or entities incorporated in India, not just any foreign entity.

questions.q: Which of the following reforms was introduced by the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021?
o: Linking of electoral roll data with Aadhaar.
questions.e: The 2021 Act enabled the linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar to curb multiple enrolments.

questions.q: What does "Psephology" refer to?
o: The scientific study of voting behaviour.
questions.e: Psephology is a branch of political science dealing with the scientific study of voting behaviour.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered the "most important factor" in voting behaviour at the local level in the Indian countryside?
questions.e: Paul Brass noted that at the local level, caste solidarity remains by far the most important factor in voting behaviour.

questions.q: What is a "wave election" according to Paul Brass?
o: An election where regional parties win all seats.
An election where the electorate develops a clear tendency in a single direction in favour of a national party/leader.
An election caused by a natural disaster.
An election with very low voter turnout.
questions.e: A wave election is based on issues that transcend local calculations and draw voters in a single direction.

questions.q: The term "anti-incumbency factor" in voting behaviour refers to:
o: Dissatisfaction with the performance of the ruling party.
questions.e: Anti-incumbency is a determinant of electoral behaviour based on dissatisfaction with the ruling party's performance.

questions.q: Technically, what does the term "coalition" (derived from the Latin 'coalitio-') mean?
questions.e: The term coalition means 'to grow together' or the act of uniting parts into one body.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of a coalition government? 1️⃣ It works on the basis of a common agreed programme. 2️⃣ Pragmatism replaces rigid dogma. 3️⃣ It is always formed before the elections.
questions.e: Coalitions work on a minimum agreed programme and are marked by pragmatism. They can be formed either before or after elections.

questions.q: Who was the Prime Minister of the first coalition government at the Centre in 1977-1979?
questions.e: Morarji Desai led the Janata Party coalition from 1977-1979.

questions.q: What is considered a "merit" of coalition governments?
o: They represent a broader spectrum of public opinion and strengthen the federal fabric.
They increase the power of the Prime Minister.
They lead to the dominance of a single ideology.
questions.e: Merits include better representation of diverse interests and strengthening federalism.

questions.q: In the context of coalition governments, what has been called the "Super-Cabinet"?
o: The Steering or Co-ordination Committee of coalition partners.
questions.e: The Steering Committee is often called a 'Super-Cabinet', which can undermine the actual cabinet.

questions.q: The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 is commonly known as:
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment Act provided for disqualification on the ground of defection and added the Tenth Schedule.

questions.q: Under the Tenth Schedule, a member of a political party becomes disqualified if:
o: They voluntarily give up their party membership.
They disagree with the leader in private.
questions.e: Disqualification occurs if a member voluntarily gives up membership or votes against party directions.

questions.q: What is the status of an "Independent member" who joins a political party after election?
o: They can join any party within six months.
There is no rule regarding independent members.
They become disqualified to remain a member.
They are rewarded with a ministry.
questions.e: An independent member becomes disqualified if they join any political party after election.

questions.q: A nominated member of a House can join a political party without disqualification if they do so:
o: They can never join a party.
Within six months of taking their seat.
Only after the House is dissolved.
questions.e: A nominated member may join a party within six months of taking their seat without inviting disqualification.

questions.q: The "split" provision (where 1/3rd members could leave without disqualification) was deleted by which Amendment Act?
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 omitted the exception for a split.

questions.q: Who is the final authority to decide on disqualification arising out of defection?
o: The Presiding Officer of the House
questions.e: Any question regarding disqualification due to defection is decided by the presiding officer.

questions.q: In the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), what did the Supreme Court rule regarding the Presiding Officer's decision on defection?
o: The Presiding Officer functions as a tribunal and the decision is subject to judicial review.
Only the Election Commission can review it.
The Speaker has no power to decide.
It is final and cannot be reviewed.
questions.e: The SC held that the presiding officer acts as a tribunal and their decision is subject to judicial review on grounds of mala fides.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment Act (2003), the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed what percentage of the Lok Sabha?
questions.e: The 91st Amendment capped the size of the Central Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: For a state, what is the minimum number of ministers (including the Chief Minister) required by the 91st Amendment?
questions.e: While the maximum is 15%, the number of ministers in a state shall not be less than 12.

questions.q: What is a "pressure group"?
o: A group that aims to capture political power.
A group of people organised to promote common interests by exerting pressure on the government.
A committee formed by the Parliament.
questions.e: Pressure groups are organised for promoting/defending common interests and influencing public policy without contesting elections.

questions.q: Which of the following is a technique used by pressure groups to influence the government? 1️⃣ Electioneering 2️⃣ Lobbying 3️⃣ Propagandising
questions.e: According to Odegard, pressure groups use electioneering, lobbying, and propagandising to secure their purposes.

questions.q: Which business group is considered one of the largest pressure groups in India?
questions.e: FICCI (Federation of Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry) is a major business pressure group.

questions.q: Match the following Trade Unions with their associated Political Parties: 1️⃣ AITUC — CPI 2️⃣ INTUC — Congress 3️⃣ BMS — BJP 4️⃣ CITU — CPM. How many are correctly matched?
questions.e: Trade unions in India are typically associated with specific political parties.

questions.q: What are "Anomic Groups" in the context of pressure groups?
o: Spontaneous breakthroughs like riots, demonstrations, and assassinations.
questions.e: Almond and Powell defined anomic groups as spontaneous breakthroughs into the political system, such as riots or assassinations.

questions.q: Which movement is an example of an ideology-based pressure group?
questions.e: Ideology-based groups pursue a cause like environmental protection (e.g., Narmada Bachao Andolan).

questions.q: According to Myron Weiner, national integration implies:
o: Establishing a single language for the whole country.
The avoidance of divisive movements and preference for national interest over parochial interests.
The fusion of all segments into one.
questions.e: Myron Weiner defined national integration as avoiding balkanisation and prioritizing national public interest.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a major obstacle to national integration in India? 1️⃣ Regionalism 2️⃣ Communalism 3️⃣ Casteism 4️⃣ Linguism
questions.e: Major obstacles include regionalism, communalism, casteism, and linguism.

questions.q: What does the "Sons of the soil theory" advocate?
o: Preference to local people in government and private jobs.
questions.e: This theory is a form of regionalism advocating preference for local people in jobs, permits, etc..

questions.q: When was the National Integration Council (NIC) first constituted?
questions.e: The NIC was constituted in 1961 following the National Integration Conference.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of the National Integration Council?
questions.e: The NIC consists of the Prime Minister as Chairman.

questions.q: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony (NFCH) is an autonomous body under which ministry?
questions.e: The NFCH is under the administrative control of the Union Home Ministry.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution directs the State to promote international peace and security?
questions.e: Article 51, a Directive Principle, directs the State to promote international peace, law, and arbitration.

questions.q: "Panchsheel," the five principles of conduct in international relations, was first signed between:
questions.e: Panchsheel was embodied in the 1954 Indo-China Treaty on Tibet.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five principles of Panchsheel?
questions.e: The principles are mutual respect, non-aggression, non-interference, equality/benefit, and peaceful co-existence.

questions.q: Why did India refuse to sign the Nuclear Non-proliferation Treaty (NPT) and the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT)?
o: Because it is not a member of the UN.
Because it considers them discriminatory and hegemonistic.
Because it wants to start a nuclear war.
questions.e: India opposes NPT/CTBT because they allow only five nations to legitimately possess nuclear weapons.

questions.q: The "Gujral Doctrine" advocates for:
o: Unilateral concessions by India to its smaller neighbours on the basis of non-reciprocity.
questions.e: The doctrine advocates India's accommodating approach toward smaller neighbours without asking for reciprocity.

questions.q: Under India's nuclear doctrine, who is the sole body authorized to use nuclear weapons?
o: The Political Council of the Nuclear Command Authority
questions.e: The Political Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, is the sole body that can authorize nuclear use.

questions.q: The "Act East Policy" was upgraded and renamed from the "Look East Policy" in which year?
questions.e: The Modi government upgraded the "Look East Policy" (initiated in 1992) to the "Act East Policy" in 2014.

questions.q: Which region of India is considered a "priority" in the Act East Policy?
questions.e: North East India is a priority, providing an interface with the ASEAN region.

questions.q: India's "Connect Central Asia" policy (2012) targets which of the following countries?
o: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan
questions.e: The policy focuses on expanding relations with five Central Asian states.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the "No First Use" posture in India's nuclear doctrine?
o: India will use nuclear weapons first in a conventional war.
India will give up its nuclear weapons to the UN.
Nuclear weapons will only be used in retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or forces.
India will never build nuclear weapons.
questions.e: "No First Use" means nuclear weapons are only for retaliation against a nuclear attack.

questions.q: What is the main objective of the "Act East Policy"?
o: To build a wall on the eastern border.
To promote economic cooperation, cultural ties, and develop strategic relationships with countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
questions.e: The policy aims for continuous engagement at bilateral, regional, and multilateral levels in Asia-Pacific.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of India's "Connect Central Asia" Policy regarding the medical field? 1️⃣ Setting up a Central Asian University in Bishkek. 2️⃣ Establishing a Central Asian e-network for tele-medicine connectivity. 3️⃣ Building world-class hospitals at competitive rates. 4️⃣ Nationalizing all private clinics in the region.
questions.e: India's policy focuses on the potential for cooperation in the medical field by setting up a Central Asian University in Bishkek and an e-network with its hub in India to deliver tele-education and tele-medicine connectivity.

questions.q: With reference to the "Act East Policy," which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It was originally conceived as a strategic military initiative. 2️⃣ It provides an interface between North East India and the ASEAN region. 3️⃣ It includes the energizing of Buddhist and Hindu links to develop new contacts.
questions.e: The Act East Policy was originally conceived as an economic initiative but gained political, strategic, and cultural dimensions. It specifically prioritizes North East India as an interface with ASEAN and seeks to energize civilizational links like Buddhist and Hindu ties.

questions.q: Under the Gujral Doctrine, what is the principle regarding the territory of South Asian countries?
o: Territory should be used to monitor the activities of neighbors.
The UN should manage all disputed territories.
Territory can be traded for economic concessions.
No South Asian country should allow its territory to be used against the interest of another country of the region.
questions.e: The second principle of the five-point roadmap in the Gujral Doctrine explicitly states that no country in the region should allow its territory to be used against another's interest.

questions.q: Which of the following is a component of India’s Nuclear Command Authority? 1️⃣ Political Council chaired by the Prime Minister. 2️⃣ Executive Council chaired by the National Security Advisor. 3️⃣ Military Council chaired by the Chief of Army Staff.
questions.e: The Nuclear Command Authority comprises a Political Council (chaired by the PM) and an Executive Council (chaired by the NSA). There is no mention of a "Military Council" as the sole authorizing body in the text.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding "Anomic" pressure groups: 1️⃣ They represent a spontaneous breakthrough into the political system. 2️⃣ Examples include Naxalite groups and the United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA). 3️⃣ They are characterized by a technocratic and anti-political frame of mind.
questions.e: Anomic groups are defined as spontaneous breakthroughs such as riots or demonstrations. The text lists Naxalite groups, JKLF, and ULFA as examples. The "technocratic" mind-set is attributed to the government/bureaucratic elite in response to these groups, not the groups themselves.

questions.q: Which of the following is a declared principle of India's foreign policy according to Article 51 of the Constitution? 1️⃣ Promotion of international peace and security. 2️⃣ Settlement of international disputes by arbitration. 3️⃣ Maintenance of just and honourable relations between nations. 4️⃣ Mandatory military alignment with global superpowers.
questions.e: Article 51 directs the state to promote peace, maintain honourable relations, foster respect for international law, and encourage settlement by arbitration. Non-alignment, rather than military alignment, is a core principle.

questions.q: In the context of the "Look East Policy," when was it first initiated and by which Prime Minister?
questions.e: The "Look East Policy" was first initiated in 1992 by the then Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a "Linguistic Group" acting as a pressure group in India? 1️⃣ Tamil Sangam 2️⃣ Anjuman Tarraki-i-Urdu 3️⃣ Hindi Sahitya Sammelan 4️⃣ Vishwa Hindu Parishad
questions.e: The text lists Tamil Sangam, Anjuman Tarraki-i-Urdu, and Hindi Sahitya Sammelan as linguistic groups. Vishwa Hindu Parishad is categorized as a religious organization.

questions.q: According to the text, why did India re-establish full diplomatic relations with South Africa in 1994?
o: As a requirement for UN membership.
Because the policy of apartheid was finally given up.
To counter the influence of the USSR.
To join a new trade bloc.
questions.e: India re-established relations in 1994 when apartheid ended and a democratic government under Nelson Mandela came into existence.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the National Integration Council (NIC): 1️⃣ It consists of the Prime Minister as Chairman. 2️⃣ It includes the Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses of Parliament. 3️⃣ Meetings are held at fixed six-month intervals.
questions.e: The NIC includes the PM as Chairman and Leaders of the Opposition. However, the text states there is no regular or specified time interval for its meetings.

questions.q: Which of the following features of a regional party is mentioned in the book? 1️⃣ It focuses on local or regional issues. 2️⃣ It identifies itself with a particular cultural, religious, or linguistic group. 3️⃣ It has a desire for greater regional autonomy of states.
questions.e: Regional parties focus on regional issues, identify with specific groups, and desire greater autonomy for states.

questions.q: With reference to the "Anti-Defection Law," what is the "Rule-Making Power"?
o: The President makes rules for the entire Parliament.
The presiding officer of a House is empowered to make rules to give effect to the Tenth Schedule.
Rules are made by a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
The Election Commission makes rules for the disqualification process.
questions.e: The presiding officer of a House is empowered to make rules regarding the Tenth Schedule, which must be placed before the House for 30 days.

questions.q: What is the "Super Prime Minister" or "Ultra Prime Minister" criticism in coalition politics?
o: The Prime Minister having too much power over the states.
The Prime Minister being elected from the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister being required to consult coalition partners before taking major decisions.
The Prime Minister serving more than two terms.
questions.e: Critics use these terms because the Prime Minister's leadership is curtailed in a coalition, requiring constant consultation with partners.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched regarding pressure groups and their categories? 1️⃣ Professional Association — Indian Medical Association 2️⃣ Student Organisation — Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad 3️⃣ Agrarian Group — Bhartiya Kisan Union
questions.e: The text correctly identifies IMA as professional , ABVP as student , and BKU as an agrarian group.

questions.q: In the Indian context, the Communist Party of India (CPI) and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPM) are examples of which type of parties?
questions.e: Political scientists describe the CPI and CPM as examples of leftist parties in India.

questions.q: What was the significance of the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988?
o: It established the National Integration Council.
It reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years.
It provided for the use of EVMs.
questions.e: The 61st Amendment Act reduced the voting age to provide the youth an opportunity to be part of the political process.

questions.q: According to the text, what is the role of "General Observers" during an election?
o: They monitor the expenditure of candidates.
They observe the poll day proceedings in critical stations.
They are responsible for law and order at the district level.
They are deployed to ensure smooth conduct and watch every stage of the electoral process.
questions.e: General Observers are deployed in adequate numbers to ensure smooth conduct and free and fair elections.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "traditional factor" mentioned as a basis for the formation of political parties in India?
questions.e: Unlike western countries, many Indian parties are formed based on traditional factors like religion, caste, language, and culture.

questions.q: What are "Electoral Bonds" designed to serve as an alternative to?
questions.e: Electoral bonds were announced as an alternative to cash donations to bring clean money and transparency into political funding.

questions.q: With reference to the "Anti-Defection Law," when does the disqualification NOT apply?
o: If an independent member joins a political party.
If a nominated member joins a party after seven months.
If a member goes out of the party as a result of a merger agreed to by two-thirds of the members.
If a member is expelled from the party for activities outside the legislature.
questions.e: Disqualification does not apply in cases of a merger where two-thirds of the party members agree.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes "Panchsheel"?
o: The five conditions for recognition as a state party.
A five-member committee for electoral reforms.
The five principles of conduct in international relations.
A five-year economic plan for India.
questions.e: Panchsheel refers to the five principles of conduct (mutual respect, non-aggression, etc.) in international relations.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the "Chief Electoral Officer" (CEO): 1️⃣ The CEO supervises election work at the district level. 2️⃣ The CEO is nominated by the Election Commission of India. 3️⃣ The CEO is an officer of the State Government/UT Administration.
questions.e: The CEO supervises work at the State/UT level , is nominated by the ECI , and is an officer of the state government. The District Election Officer (DEO) supervises the district.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated "dysfunction" of regional parties in India?
o: They are responsible for the non-resolution of inter-state water and border disputes.
They provide better governance at the regional level.
They increase political consciousness among the people.
questions.e: One of the negative points listed is that regional parties are responsible for the unresolution of inter-state disputes.

questions.q: What is the "First-past-the-post" system used for in India?
o: Elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Allocation of symbols to unrecognised parties.
questions.e: India uses the first-past-the-post electoral system for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections.

questions.q: Which of the following organizations is categorized as an "Ideology Based Group" in India?
questions.e: Narmada Bachao Andolan and the Chipko Movement are examples of groups formed to pursue a particular ideology or cause (environmental protection).

questions.q: In 1997, the security deposit for contesting the election of the President of India was increased to:
questions.e: The security deposit was increased from ₹2,500 to ₹15,000 for both the President and Vice-President to discourage frivolous candidates.

questions.q: What is the "Gujral Doctrine" principle regarding non-interference?
o: The UN should interfere in all internal disputes.
Interference is allowed if requested by a political party.
No South Asian country should interfere in the internal affairs of another country.
India has the right to interfere in smaller countries for peace.
questions.e: The third principle of the Gujral Doctrine roadmap is that no country should interfere in the internal affairs of another.

questions.q: With reference to the "Act East Policy," which statement is correct regarding ASEAN?
o: ASEAN countries are excluded from the "Make in India" initiative.
India has decreased its economic engagement with ASEAN since 2014.
The ASEAN-India Agreement on Trade in Service and Investments entered into force in 2015.
India has no strategic security interest in the ASEAN region.
questions.e: India's economic engagement has been stepped up, and the agreement on trade and services entered into force on July 1, 2015.

questions.q: According to the text, what is "Linguism"?
o: Love for one's language and language-speaking people.
The official translation of the Constitution.
A mandatory three-language formula in schools.
questions.e: Linguism is defined as love for one's language and people, often resulting from the political process.

questions.q: Which committee was appointed in 2010 to look into the whole gamut of election laws and electoral reforms?
questions.e: The Tankha Committee (Core Committee) was appointed in 2010 for this purpose.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the "District Election Officer" (DEO): 1️⃣ The DEO is nominated by the Election Commission of India. 2️⃣ The DEO appoints the Presiding Officers and Polling Officers. 3️⃣ The DEO is an officer of the Central Government.
questions.e: The DEO is a State Government officer nominated by the ECI and is responsible for appointing Presiding and Polling officers.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the "Connect Central Asia" Policy?
o: Withdrawing all Indian banks from the region.
Building strong political relations through high-level visits.
questions.e: On the contrary, the policy suggests that Indian banks can expand their presence if they see a favourable environment.

questions.q: What is the "National Foundation for Communal Harmony" (NFCH)?
o: A forum for resolving water disputes.
An autonomous body that provides assistance to child victims of societal violence.
A political party based on religious harmony.
questions.e: The NFCH promotes communal harmony and provides financial assistance to child victims for their care and education.

questions.q: According to the text, when were Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) first used in general elections for an entire state?
questions.e: EVMs were first used in the general elections for the entire state of Goa in 1999.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the "First General Elections" (1952) is correct?
o: Electronic Voting Machines were used for the first time.
The Bharatiya Janata Party was the main opposition.
The Indian National Congress won 364 seats.
questions.e: In the first general elections, the Congress won 364 seats. There were 14 national parties at the time.

questions.q: What does "Communalism" mean in the context of Indian politics?
o: The formation of groups based on professional skills.
Love for one's religious community in preference to the nation.
questions.e: Communalism is defined as promoting communal interest at the cost of other religious communities and the nation.

questions.q: With reference to "Electoral Reforms," what was the "Booth Capturing" provision of 1989?
o: It made booth capturing a legal method of protest.
It provided for adjournment of poll or countermanding of elections in case of booth capturing.
It defined booth capturing as a minor offense.
It required all polling stations to be captured by the military.
questions.e: In 1989, a provision was made to adjourn or countermand elections if booth capturing occurred.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "merit" of coalition governments mentioned in the text?
o: Faster decision-making by the Prime Minister.
Ending the role of regional parties.
Reduction in the size of the Council of Ministers.
questions.e: Coalition governments lead to consensus-based politics as policies require the concurrence of all partners.

questions.q: What is the "None of the Above" (NOTA) provision based on?
o: A recommendation by the Vohra Committee.
A law passed by the Parliament in 1951.
Directions of the Supreme Court of India.
questions.e: The ECI made the NOTA provision according to the directions of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Under the "Act East Policy," which two civilizational links are being energized?
questions.e: On the civilizational front, Buddhist and Hindu links are being energized to develop new contacts.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a "Tribal Organisation" as a pressure group?
questions.e: The People's Liberation Army in Manipur is listed as a tribal organisation.

questions.q: What is the "Jumbo Ministry" reference regarding the A.B. Vajpayee ministry of 1999?
o: A ministry that focused on elephant conservation.
A ministry formed by only one party.
A ministry where the PM had total power.
A ministry with over 70 ministers due to coalition requirements.
questions.e: The 1999 ministry was called a 'Jumbo Ministry' because it had 70-plus ministers to reflect all coalition constituents.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for re-fixing the number of seats reserved for SC and ST on the basis of the 2001 census?
questions.e: Articles 330 and 332 provide for re-fixing seats reserved for SCs and STs.

questions.q: According to the Gujral Doctrine, how should South Asian countries settle their disputes?
o: Through the intervention of a global superpower.
questions.e: The fifth principle of the Gujral Doctrine states that all South Asian countries should settle disputes through peaceful bilateral negotiations.

questions.q: What is the "One-Dominant Party System" also referred to by Rajni Kothari?
questions.e: Rajni Kothari preferred to call the Indian party system the 'Congress system' due to its long period of dominance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "Technique" of pressure groups mentioned in the book?
questions.e: Pressure groups influence the government through legitimate methods like lobbying, publicity, and petitioning.

questions.q: When was the "Act East Policy" officially launched by the Modi Government?
questions.e: The Modi Government renamed and upgraded the policy in 2014.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment, a disqualified defector is also disqualified from:
questions.e: A member disqualified on the ground of defection is also disqualified from being appointed as a minister.

questions.q: What does the "No First Use" nuclear posture imply?
o: India will use nuclear weapons only in retaliation.
India will never use nuclear weapons.
Nuclear weapons are controlled by the military alone.
India will be the first to use nuclear weapons in South Asia.
questions.e: The posture states that nuclear weapons will only be used in retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or forces.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an "Anomic" pressure group?
questions.e: Dal Khalsa is listed under anomic pressure groups.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the "Model Code of Conduct"?
o: It only applies to the opposition parties.
It was effectively first put to use in 1991 to ensure fair elections.
It has been a law since 1951.
It is issued by the President of India.
questions.e: The Election Commission first effectively used the Model Code of Conduct in 1991 to ensure a level playing field.

questions.q: What is the "Connect Central Asia" Policy element regarding the "International North-South Transport Corridor"?
o: India has reactivated the corridor for land connectivity.
The corridor is only for military use.
The corridor connects India to Australia.
questions.e: As part of the policy, India has reactivated the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) for land connectivity.

questions.q: Which of the following committees recommended state funding of elections?
questions.e: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) upheld the argument for the introduction of state funding of elections.

questions.q: According to the text, what is the role of "Police Observers" in an election?
o: They monitor force deployment and law and order situations.
They count the votes at the polling station.
questions.e: Police Observers (IPS officers) monitor force deployment and co-ordinate between civil and police administrations.

questions.q: Which of the following regional parties was formed by a split in a national party?
questions.e: Rashtriya Janata Dal is listed as a regional party formed by a split in a national party.

questions.q: What does "Panchsheel" principle "Peaceful co-existence" imply?
o: All nations must have the same government.
All internal affairs are managed by the UN.
Nations with different systems can live together in peace.
India will only co-exist with its allies.
questions.e: Peaceful co-existence is the fifth principle of Panchsheel.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of "Voting Behaviour" mentioned in the book?
o: It is only determined by economic conditions.
It is a form of military behaviour.
It has no significance in a democracy.
It reflects a voter's choices, preferences, and ideologies.
questions.e: Voting behaviour reflects the choices, preferences, ideologies, and concerns of voters.

questions.q: Under the "Act East Policy," which region of India is a "priority"?
questions.e: The North East of India has been a priority in the Act East Policy.

questions.q: What is "Casteism" in the context of national integration?
o: A scientific study of different castes.
The promotion of inter-caste marriages only.
The abolition of all caste identities.
Love for one's own caste-group in preference to national interest.
questions.e: Casteism implies love for one's own caste-group at the cost of the general national interest.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment, what is a "remunerative political post"?
o: An office under the Government where salary is paid out of public revenue.
Any post with a high salary in a private company.
A post in a non-governmental organization.
A volunteer position in a political party.
questions.e: It means an office under the government or a government-owned body where remuneration is paid by that body or the public revenue.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "principle" of India's foreign policy?
questions.e: Anti-racialism, anti-colonialism, and the promotion of world peace are key principles.

questions.q: What is the role of "Micro Observers" during the election poll day?
o: They oversee the work of the Chief Electoral Officer.
They are responsible for the media passes.
They observe poll proceedings in critical/vulnerable polling stations.
They monitor the overall expenditure of the state.
questions.e: Micro Observers are chosen from Central Government/PSU officials to monitor critical polling stations.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of the Anti-Defection Law?
o: It reduces corruption at the political level.
It provides for greater stability in the body politic.
It guarantees that every legislator will become a minister.
It gives constitutional recognition to political parties.
questions.e: Advantages include stability, constitutional recognition of parties, and reduced corruption.

questions.q: What is the "Gujral Doctrine" principle regarding territorial integrity?
o: All South Asian countries should respect each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty.
India will only respect the integrity of its allies.
Territorial disputes must be settled by force.
Sovereignty is secondary to economic profit.
questions.e: The fourth principle of the roadmap is respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty.

questions.q: Under the "Connect Central Asia" Policy, which area offers "huge potential for cooperation"?
questions.e: The medical field is specifically noted as having huge potential for cooperation.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about "Electoral Rolls" is correct?
o: Names of those who turn 18 on the 1st January are added.
They are revised every five years only.
The roll is prepared by the Prime Minister's office.
Only property owners can be on the roll.
questions.e: The electoral roll is normally revised every year to add names of those turning 18 on January 1st.

questions.q: Which organization is an example of an "Agrarian Group" pressure group?
questions.e: The All India Kisan Sabha is described as the oldest and largest agrarian group.

questions.q: According to the text, when did India re-establish full diplomatic relations with South Africa?
questions.e: Full diplomatic relations were re-established in 1994 after the policy of apartheid ended.

questions.q: What is the "Super Prime Minister" criticism often directed at?
o: A Prime Minister with a two-thirds majority.
The Chief Minister of a state.
A Prime Minister in a coalition government.
questions.e: Critics use this term in a coalition context because the PM must consult partners on major decisions.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding "Electoral Reforms" since 2010?
o: Voting rights were given to citizens living abroad.
The voting age was increased to 21.
questions.e: In 2010, a provision was made to confer voting rights to citizens of India residing outside the country.

questions.q: What does "Panchsheel" principle "Non-aggression" mean?
o: Nations should not attack each other.
India will only attack its neighbors.
Aggression is allowed if the UN permits.
questions.e: Non-aggression is the second principle of the five principles of conduct.

questions.q: Which of the following regional parties is categorized as "Personalised"?
o: Parties formed by leaders based on their charismatic personality.
questions.e: The fourth category of regional parties consists of those formed by leaders based on their charismatic personality; they are called personalised parties.

questions.q: Under the "Act East Policy," which type of links are being energized between people?
questions.e: Civilizationally, Buddhist and Hindu links are being energized to develop new contacts.

questions.q: What is the "National Integration Council" (NIC) purpose?
o: To find ways to combat evils like communalism and regionalism.
To build new highways across states.
questions.e: The NIC was set up to review matters pertaining to national integration and combat communalism, casteism, regionalism, and linguism.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment, what happens to a defector regarding "public offices"?
o: They are promoted to a higher post.
They are debarred from holding any remunerative political post for the remaining term.
They can hold any office if the President permits.
They are only debarred if they belong to a regional party.
questions.e: A disqualified member is also disqualified from holding any remunerative political post for the duration of the remaining term or until fresh elections.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "principle" of India's foreign policy regarding the world?
questions.e: Promotion of international peace and security is a core principle of Indian foreign policy.

questions.q: What is the "Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail" (VVPAT) system attached to?
questions.e: VVPAT is an independent system attached with the EVMs that allows voters to verify their cast votes.

questions.q: Which of the following regional parties has an "all-India outlook but lacks a national electoral base"?
questions.e: Samajwadi Party and Nationalist Congress Party are examples of regional parties with an all-India outlook but limited base.

questions.q: Under the "Connect Central Asia" Policy, what is the "synergy of joint efforts" focus?
o: SCO, Eurasian Economic Community, and the Custom Union.
NASA and the European Space Agency.
questions.e: India seeks to step up multilateral engagement using synergies through fora like the SCO and EEC.

questions.q: What is "Regionalism" in the context of obstacles to national integration?
o: Support for a strong central government.
Love for the country as a whole.
questions.e: Regionalism refers to sub-national loyalty, often preferring a particular region over the country as a whole.

questions.q: Which committee was headed by M.N. Venkatachaliah in 2000-2002?
o: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution
questions.e: M.N. Venkatachaliah headed the NCRWC.

questions.q: What is the "No First Use" nuclear doctrine's exception?
o: India will retain the option of nuclear retaliation in case of a major attack by biological or chemical weapons.
India will use nuclear weapons first against any non-nuclear state.
There are no exceptions to the "No First Use" rule.
India will use nuclear weapons first in a border dispute.
questions.e: In the event of a major attack by biological or chemical weapons, India retains the option of nuclear retaliation.

questions.q: Which of the following organizations is a "Professional Association" pressure group?
questions.e: Indian Medical Association (IMA) is listed as a professional association.

questions.q: According to the text, when did the "Model Code of Conduct" first come into effective use?
questions.e: The ECI first effectively used the Model Code of Conduct in 1991 to ensure fair elections.

questions.q: What is "Anti-Colonialism" in India's foreign policy?
o: Opposition to colonialism and imperialism in all forms.
A policy that supports colonial rule.
A policy focused only on South Asian borders.
questions.e: India views colonialism as leading to exploitation and hindering world peace, therefore opposing it in all forms.

questions.q: Which of the following regional parties was formed by "individual leaders on the basis of their charismatic personality"?
questions.e: These are called personalised parties and are often short-lived.

questions.q: Under the "Act East Policy," which two links are being "energized" on the civilization front?
questions.e: Buddhist and Hindu links are being energized to develop new contacts.

questions.q: What is the "National Foundation for Communal Harmony" (NFCH) primary mission?
o: To build new temples and mosques.
To provide assistance to child victims of societal violence.
To count the total population of religious groups.
questions.e: The NFCH promotes communal harmony and helps child victims of societal violence.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment, the total number of ministers in a state shall not exceed what percentage of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.e: The total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.

questions.q: What is the "None of the Above" (NOTA) option's main purpose?
o: To allow the government to appoint a winner.
To count the number of voters who stayed home.
To cancel the votes of the winning candidate.
To allow voters to exercise the right not to vote for any candidate while maintaining secrecy.
questions.e: NOTA allows voters to express dissatisfaction with all candidates in the fray secretly.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding "Electoral Bonds"?
o: They can be encashed by eligible parties only through an authorized bank account.
They can be bought with cash anonymously up to any amount.
They can be used for making donations to any newly registered party.
They carry the name of the buyer on the face of the bond.
questions.e: Bonds can only be encashed by parties that secured at least 1% of votes in the last election via an authorized bank.

questions.q: Under the "Connect Central Asia" Policy, what area of cooperation offers potential for synergy using the "Central Asian e-network"?
questions.e: The e-network with its hub in India is meant to deliver tele-education and tele-medicine connectivity.

questions.q: What is "Casteism" as an obstacle to national integration?
o: The elimination of caste identities from the electoral roll.
The promotion of social welfare for all.
Love for one's own caste-group in preference to national interest.
questions.e: Casteism implies prioritizing one's caste interest over general national interest, often through politicisation.

questions.q: According to the text, what is the role of "General Observers" in an election?
o: To count the votes in the district.
To issue the notification for elections.
To watch every stage of the electoral process and ensure free and fair elections.
questions.e: General Observers are deployed by the ECI to ensure smooth conduct and fairness in elections.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of "Voting Behaviour" in India?
o: It is strictly controlled by the Election Commission.
It is influenced by multiple factors like caste, religion, and personality.
It has no impact on the outcome of the government.
It is only determined by the weather on the polling day.
questions.e: Voting behaviour in India is influenced by factors like caste, religion, language, region, and charismatic personality.

questions.q: Under the "Act East Policy," which initiative is focused on infrastructure and trade cooperation with ASEAN?
questions.e: The policy emphasizes India-ASEAN cooperation in agendas like infrastructure, manufacturing, and "Make in India".

questions.q: What is the "Gujral Doctrine" principle regarding South Asian countries' internal affairs?
o: The UN should have the final say in internal disputes.
Neighboring countries should allow external interference for peace.
No country should interfere in the internal affairs of another.
India should manage the internal affairs of its smaller neighbors.
questions.e: Non-interference in the internal affairs of other countries is a core principle of the Gujral Doctrine.

questions.q: Which of the following regional parties was formed due to "cultural and ethnic pluralism"?
o: Parties like Akali Dal and DMK
questions.e: Cultural and ethnic pluralism is a primary reason for the emergence of regional parties in India.

questions.q: Under the "Connect Central Asia" Policy, what field allows Indian companies to showcase their capability at "competitive rates"?
questions.e: Indian companies can showcase their capability in the construction sector and build world-class structures.

questions.q: What is the "National Integration Council" (NIC) consists of?
o: The Chief Election Commissioner and all District Magistrates.
The Chief Justice and all High Court judges.
Prime Minister, Union Ministers, CMs, and Leaders of the Opposition.
questions.e: The NIC includes the PM, Union Ministers, LoP, and Chief Ministers of all states and UTs with legislatures.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment, what happens to a defector regarding "remunerative political posts"?
o: They are only debarred if they are from a national party.
They can hold any post except for a ministry.
They are debarred from holding any such post for the duration of the remaining term.
They can hold a post if it is in a private-public partnership.
questions.e: A member disqualified for defection is also disqualified from holding any remunerative political post.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "principle" of India's foreign policy regarding "Afro-Asian Bias"?
o: Support for European dominance over Afro-Asian states.
Special bias towards Afro-Asian nations to promote unity and influence.
questions.e: India's foreign policy has always exhibited a special bias towards the Afro-Asian nations, seeking international assistance for their development.

questions.q: What is the "Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail" (VVPAT) slip display duration?
questions.e: When a vote is cast, the slip remains exposed for seven seconds before falling into the sealed dropbox.

questions.q: Which of the following regional parties is categorized as being formed by a "split in national parties"?
questions.e: Trinamool Congress, RJD, and BJD are examples of parties formed due to splits in national parties.

questions.q: Under the "Connect Central Asia" Policy, which area offers Synergies through "high level visits"?
questions.e: India seeks to build on strong political relations through the exchange of high-level visits.

questions.q: What is "Linguism" as an obstacle to national integration?
o: Love for one's language and language-speaking people.
A mandatory one-language policy for the entire nation.
The study of foreign languages only.
questions.e: Linguism is a consequence of the political process and love for one's language people.

questions.q: According to the text, what is the role of "Police Observers" in an election?
o: To monitor force deployment and law and order.
questions.e: IPS officers are deployed as Police Observers to monitor force deployment and law and order.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the "Anti-Defection Law"?
o: It allows "retail" defections but legalises "wholesale" defections.
It has been 100% effective in stopping all defections.
It was introduced in the 1st General Election.
It only applies to the Rajya Sabha.
questions.e: Critics argue the law banned only retail (individual) defections while legalising wholesale (bulk) defections.

questions.q: What does the "No First Use" nuclear doctrine's "retaliation" imply?
o: Retaliation will only use conventional weapons.
Retaliation will be minor and diplomatic.
India will not retaliate if the attacker is an ally.
Retaliation will be massive and designed to inflict unacceptable damage.
questions.e: Nuclear retaliation to a first strike will be massive and designed to inflict unacceptable damage.

questions.q: Which organization is an example of an "Ideology Based Group"?
questions.e: Narmada Bachao Andolan and the Chipko Movement are ideology-based pressure groups.

questions.q: Under the "Act East Policy," what is the objective regarding ASEAN?
o: To promote economic cooperation and strategic relationships.
To isolate the North East from ASEAN.
To reduce trade with ASEAN countries.
To replace regional languages with English.
questions.e: The objective is economic cooperation, cultural ties, and strategic relationships through continuous engagement.

questions.q: What is the "National Foundation for Communal Harmony" (NFCH) mission?
o: To provide financial assistance to child victims of societal violence.
To manage the national integration council.
questions.e: The NFCH promotes communal harmony and helps rehabilitate child victims of violence.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment, the total number of ministers in the Central Council shall not exceed:
questions.e: The total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: What is the "None of the Above" (NOTA) option's main purpose?
o: To count the number of informal votes.
To allow the government to choose the winner.
To reject all candidates while maintaining ballot secrecy.
questions.e: NOTA allows voters who decide not to vote for any candidate in the fray to exercise their right while maintaining secrecy.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding "Electoral Bonds"?
o: They are issued in denominations of ₹500 and ₹2,000.
They can be encashed by any registered political party.
They can be bought by any foreign citizen.
They do not carry the name of the buyer or payee.
questions.e: Electoral bonds are bearer banking instruments and do not carry the name of the buyer or payee.

questions.q: Under the "Connect Central Asia" Policy, what field allows Synergies through "military training"?
questions.e: Synergies focus on military training, joint research, and counter-terrorism coordination.

questions.q: What is "Regionalism" as an obstacle to national integration?
o: Love for the nation as a whole.
Support for a strong central government.
questions.e: Regionalism refers to sub-national loyalty, often favoring a specific region over the country.

questions.q: According to the text, what is the role of "Micro Observers" in an election?
o: To oversee the state election commission.
To observe poll proceedings in critical polling stations on poll day.
To verify the assets of candidates.
questions.e: Micro Observers are chosen from Central Government/PSU officials to monitor critical polling stations.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding "Voting Behaviour" in India?
o: It is influenced by charismatic personality of leaders.
It has no significance in the political development.
It is only determined by the voter's age.
questions.e: The charismatic personality of party leaders like Nehru, Indira Gandhi, and Narendra Modi has significantly influenced electorate.

questions.q: Under the "Act East Policy," which region of India provides an "interface" with the ASEAN region?
questions.e: The policy provides an interface between North East India and the ASEAN region.

questions.q: What is "Communalism" in the context of obstacles to national integration?
o: The promotion of social welfare for all religions.
A scientific study of religious texts.
Love for one's religious community in preference to the nation.
questions.e: Communalism implies promoting one's religious interest at the cost of other communities and the nation.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment, a disqualified defector is also:
o: Disqualified from holding any remunerative political post.
Allowed to contest as an independent immediately.
questions.e: A disqualified member is also disqualified from holding any remunerative political post for the remaining term.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "principle" of India's foreign policy?
questions.e: India opposes colonialism and imperialism as they lead to exploitation and hinder peace.

questions.q: What is the "Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail" (VVPAT) system purpose?
o: To allow voters to verify that their votes are cast as intended.
To print the final election result.
To count the total number of voters.
questions.e: VVPAT is an independent system attached with EVMs allowing voters to verify their cast vote.
